tts_summary:
Here's your after-the-close earnings wrap for Tuesday, October 6th. Four names to run through — let's get into it.

First up, Penguin Solutions. This one's clean and straightforward — a strong beat-and-raise. Fiscal Q4 EPS came in at a dollar versus the Street at seventy-seven cents, and revenue printed at five hundred sixty-seven million against five-twenty expected. But the real story is the raised fiscal twenty-twenty-seven outlook. They now see sales up roughly forty percent for the year, up from a prior thirty percent guide, and EPS up around fifty-five percent versus the prior thirty. Management pointed directly to accelerating AI Infrastructure momentum as the catalyst. This is a name the market is going to reward.

Next, ZIM Integrated Shipping. ZIM raised its full-year EBITDA guidance to two-point-seven to three billion dollars, versus the prior range of two to two-point-four billion. This is the second major upside preannouncement from a large shipping name after Maersk made a similar move. The message is clear — resilient global demand combined with geopolitical disruption is sending freight rates and volumes soaring, and that's creating a powerful and broad tailwind across the container shipping sector. This isn't a one-off company story. It's a sector re-rate in progress.

Now Constellation Brands — this one's more nuanced. The headline beat looks good: fiscal Q2 EPS of three-seventy-four versus three-fifty-three expected, beer volumes up five-point-five percent which was about three hundred forty basis points above consensus, and beer margins down one hundred sixty basis points year over year — but that was better than feared. So the execution was solid. The problem is two-fold. Beer depletions — the real demand signal — came in only inline, down point-six percent year over year. And despite the Q2 outperformance, management left full-year guidance completely unchanged across EPS, sales, margins, and cash flow. That's going to temper any enthusiasm. They also announced a bolt-on acquisition of SpikedAde for seventy-five million dollars upfront plus up to two-seventy-eight million in contingent payments over five years. Interesting strategic move but not a needle-mover here. Net-net, this is a mixed read — execution yes, but no upgrade to the full-year view is a headwind.

Finally, Fair Isaac — FICO — got a meaningful endorsement today. United Wholesale Mortgage, the number-one mortgage lender in the country, reaffirmed its commitment to using FICO Scores on all credit pulls across its broker operations. In a world where alternative scoring models are getting more attention, this is a real vote of confidence in FICO's market position and reinforces the company's moat in mortgage origination.

Bottom line for the session: AI infrastructure spending remains red-hot — Penguin Solutions confirms it. Shipping is in a genuine upcycle. Constellation executed but didn't raise, which sets up a tricky open. And FICO's competitive position just got reaffirmed by the biggest player in the mortgage market.
